blocks.body: {"level":"B2","intro":"Conditionals with Unless, Provided That, and As Long As: Conditionals with unless, provided that, and as long as gives precise B2 condition meanings: if not, only if, and while the condition remains true.","rules":[{"label":"Unless","text":"Unless usually means if not.","example":"Unless you hurry, you will miss the train."},{"label":"Provided that","text":"Provided that makes the condition explicit and restrictive.","example":"You can join provided that you register today."},{"label":"As long as","text":"As long as means only if the condition continues to be true.","example":"You can stay as long as you are quiet."}]}

blocks.body: {"level":"C1","intro":"Advanced Conditionals: compact C1 anchors for mixed conditionals, formal condition markers, and careful conditional inversion.","rules":[{"label":"Past to present result","text":"Use if + past perfect with would + base form or would be + -ing for a present result.","example":"If I had accepted the offer, I would be working abroad now."},{"label":"Present to past result","text":"Use if + past simple with would have + past participle for a past result.","example":"If she were more organized, she would have submitted the report on time."},{"label":"Formal markers and inversion","text":"Use provided that, as long as, unless, and limited had-inversion where the meaning is clear.","example":"Had I known earlier, I would have acted differently."}]}

page.title: Conditional Alternatives And Nuance
page.subtitle_html: Conditional Alternatives And Nuance - C2 condition/result language with provided that, otherwise, but for, and formal inversion.
page.subtitle_text: C2 condition/result language with provided that, otherwise, but for, and formal inversion.

blocks.body: {"level":"C2","intro":"Conditional alternatives and nuance: concise C2 anchors for formal and nuanced condition/result structures.","rules":[{"label":"Condition markers","text":"Use provided that, assuming, supposing, and on condition that to state precise requirements.","example":"We will proceed provided that the terms are acceptable."},{"label":"Absent cause","text":"Use but for, were it not for, and had it not been for to show that one factor changes the whole result.","example":"But for the delay, the report would be ready."},{"label":"Formal inversion","text":"Use should + subject + base verb or were + subject + to + base verb for formal hypothetical conditions.","example":"Should you need assistance, contact the coordinator."}]}
